heading.en: A cricket ball in a stadium

hook.en: If an atom were the size of the Chinnaswamy stadium, its nucleus would be smaller than a marble at the centre, yet it holds almost all the mass.
hook.kn: ಪರಮಾಣು ಚಿನ್ನಸ್ವಾಮಿ ಕ್ರೀಡಾಂಗಣದಷ್ಟು ದೊಡ್ಡದಾದರೆ, ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯಸ್ ಮಧ್ಯದ ಒಂದು ಗೋಲಿಗಿಂತ ಚಿಕ್ಕದು; ಆದರೂ ಬಹುತೇಕ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಅದರಲ್ಲೇ.

objectives.en: Show that nuclear density is independent of A

narration.en: If an atom were the size of the Chinnaswamy stadium, its nucleus would be smaller than a marble at the centre, yet it holds almost all the mass.
narration.kn: ಪರಮಾಣು ಚಿನ್ನಸ್ವಾಮಿ ಕ್ರೀಡಾಂಗಣದಷ್ಟು ದೊಡ್ಡದಾದರೆ, ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯಸ್ ಮಧ್ಯದ ಒಂದು ಗೋಲಿಗಿಂತ ಚಿಕ್ಕದು; ಆದರೂ ಬಹುತೇಕ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಅದರಲ್ಲೇ.

body.en: Scattering experiments with fast electrons and alpha particles show that the radius of a nucleus of mass number $A$ is $R = R_0A^{1/3}$, with $R_0 \approx 1.2$ fm ($1$ fm $= 10^{-15}$ m). So the volume of a nucleus is proportional to $A$.
body.kn: A ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯಸ್‌ನ ತ್ರಿಜ್ಯ R = R₀A^(1/3), R₀ ≈ 1.2 fm. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಘನಫಲ A ಗೆ ಅನುಪಾತೀಯ.

narration.en: Scattering experiments with fast electrons and alpha particles show that the radius of a nucleus of mass number A is R = R_0A^{1/3}, with R_0 \approx 1.2 fm (1 fm = 10^{-15} m). So the volume of a nucleus is proportional to A.
narration.kn: A ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯಸ್‌ನ ತ್ರಿಜ್ಯ R = R₀A^(1/3), R₀ ≈ 1.2 fm. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಘನಫಲ A ಗೆ ಅನುಪಾತೀಯ.

title.en: Board: how big is a nucleus?

narration.en: Let us see how nuclear size grows with mass number and why all nuclei have the same density.

say.en: The radius grows as the cube root of A, with R₀ about 1.2 femtometre.
Aluminium-27: cube root of 27 is 3, so R = 3.6 fm. Eight times the nucleons gives only twice the radius.
Mass is A times m and volume is four-thirds π R₀³ A, so A cancels in the density.

text.en: A cancels: same for all nuclei

say.en: The density is about 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg per cubic metre, some 10¹⁴ times that of water.

body.en: The mass of a nucleus is about $A$ u and its volume is $\tfrac43\pi R_0^3A$, so the density does not depend on $A$. It is about $2.3\times10^{17}$ kg/m³, roughly $10^{14}$ times the density of water. Neutron stars are made of matter this dense.
body.kn: ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯಸ್‌ನ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಮತ್ತು ಘನಫಲ ಎರಡೂ A ಗೆ ಅನುಪಾತೀಯ; ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಸಾಂದ್ರತೆ ಸ್ಥಿರ, ಸುಮಾರು 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³.

narration.en: The mass of a nucleus is about A u and its volume is \tfrac43\pi R_0^3A, so the density does not depend on A. It is about 2.3\times10^{17} kg/m³, roughly 10^{14} times the density of water. Neutron stars are made of matter this dense.
narration.kn: ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯಸ್‌ನ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಮತ್ತು ಘನಫಲ ಎರಡೂ A ಗೆ ಅನುಪಾತೀಯ; ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಸಾಂದ್ರತೆ ಸ್ಥಿರ, ಸುಮಾರು 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³.

title.en: Try it: nuclear radius and density

narration.en: Slide the mass number from light to heavy nuclei; watch the radius and the density.

caption.en: R = 1.2 A^(1/3) fm. The radius grows slowly with A, but the density stays the same.

tryThis.en: Compare A = 27 and A = 216. What is the ratio of radii?
Does the density change from hydrogen to uranium?
Which A gives a radius of 6 fm?

problem.en: Find the radius of the ²⁷Al nucleus and its density. (R₀ = 1.2 fm, 1 u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg)

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the radius of the ²⁷Al nucleus and its density. (R₀ = 1.2 fm, 1 u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg)

body.en: Radius ratios are cube roots of mass-number ratios. Look for perfect cubes: 8, 27, 64, 125, 216. ²⁷Al : ⁶⁴Cu : ¹²⁵Te radii are 3 : 4 : 5.

narration.en: Cube-root ratios. Radius ratios are cube roots of mass-number ratios. Look for perfect cubes: 8, 27, 64, 125, 216. ²⁷Al : ⁶⁴Cu : ¹²⁵Te radii are 3 : 4 : 5.

mnemonic.en: R grows as the cube root of A.

points.en: Nuclear volume is proportional to A.
Nuclear density ≈ 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³ for all nuclei.
